content.comment_body: Good morning, I came across this post and am looking for a detailed explanation on how to operate the backlights. Specifically, I am interested in knowing: 1. How many color options there are? 2. Is it possible to make the display flash or switch between colors? Any additional information would be appreciated. --- Split from [product_name] [product_name] [version_no] - where to set the backlight color.

Backlight flags: Flags M25, M28, and M29 are used to control the backlight of the onboard display. Flags M26, M30, and M31 manage the backlight for the [product_name] operator device. The outputs from timers, message texts, or other function blocks can be used to activate the backlight flags. You can set up several function blocks either in sequence or parallel to allow multiple conditions to manage backlight control. M25 corresponds to a white backlight. M28 activates an amber backlight. M29 triggers a red backlight. For the operator device: M26 results in white backlight. M30 switches to amber backlight. M31 enables red backlight. When flags are connected in parallel, the color associated with the highest marker number will take priority. If you use markers M25, M28, or M29 within the logic, automatic backlighting for the onboard display via cursor keys will be disabled. Similarly, using M26, M30, or M31 means the operator device's backlighting won't switch on automatically via button presses. Refer to the provided attachment for further details.
